title: Registrar's Office graduate curriculum review rules
description: Machine-readable checks derived from 2 years of Registrar workflow comments (2024-07..2026-07). Each rule: what to check on a program proposal, why, and how the Registrar phrases the correction. Intended for Claude to pre-screen a proposal before it enters CIM workflow. severity: block = will be rolled back; fix = Registrar will edit; advisory = context.

source.scope: graduate programs in CIM workflow (active + completed)

rules.rule: Effective catalog edition must equal the catalog year of the effective term (Fall YYYY -> YYYY-(YYYY+1)).
rules.check: Compare effective term to effective catalog edition; flag mismatch.
rules.why: Catalog edition is defined by the effective (Fall) term.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: Effective catalog edition corrected from 2025-2026 to 2026-2027, per proposed effective term (Fall 2026).

rules.rule: Program-requirement changes are effective on a catalog-year (Fall) basis only; the effective term cannot be a Spring/Summer term for requirement changes.
rules.check: If the proposal changes program requirements and the effective term is not a Fall term, flag it.
rules.why: Requirement changes apply per catalog year.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: Eff term updated from Spring 2026 to Fall 2026, as program requirement changes can only be made on a catalog year basis.

rules.rule: There is an annual college-approval deadline per catalog year; proposals approved after it are moved to the next catalog edition.
rules.check: If submitting late in a cycle, expect the edition to roll forward.

example.author: ben.joseph
example.quote: As the deadline for college approval of program proposals for 2026-2027 implementation has passed, the Registrar's Office has changed the effective catalog edition of this proposal to 2027-2028.

rules.rule: New degree programs requiring Faculty Senate/Board approval may be pushed to a later term/edition, but can appear in a catalog addendum if fully approved before publication.
rules.check: New-degree proposals: confirm Senate/Board timing vs effective term.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: Effective term moved from Fall 2026 to Spring 2027 ... given the need for Senate and Board approval ... included in that addendum.

rules.rule: Campus-specific program records must include the campus in parentheses in the full program title, e.g. '(Boston)'.
rules.check: Full title of a campus-specific record lacks a '(Campus)' suffix.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: ' (Boston)' added to full program title for campus-specific program record projects.

rules.rule: Minors do NOT carry a campus parenthetical in the title.
rules.check: A Minor title contains a '(Campus)' suffix.
rules.why: Minors are not campus-specific in the catalog.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: '(New York)' removed [from] full program title, as Northeastern minors will not have a [campus].

rules.rule: Online programs use the standard '(Online)' title; the '(Online - Vancouver Requirements)' form is a one-off regulatory case, not a model.
rules.check: New online program proposing a non-standard online parenthetical.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: ...should not be a model for future online programs.

rules.rule: Remove implied promises of student achievement/outcomes from the overview.
rules.check: Overview contains outcome guarantees ('prepares students to...', 'will be able to...', 'option to deepen learning').
rules.why: Catalog overviews describe the program, not guarantee results.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: Overview has been modified ... to remove implied promises of student achievement.

rules.rule: Overview must not imply the curriculum includes remedial or undergraduate coursework.
rules.check: Overview references prep/Align courses as part of the degree curriculum.
rules.why: Graduate curriculum should not read as remedial.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: removed ... to avoid inadvertently implying that the curriculum includes remedial or undergraduate coursework: 'The Align courses prepare students for the MS AI degree.'

rules.rule: Overview must state whether a concentration is optional or required, consistent with the requirements section.
rules.check: Concentration optionality in overview disagrees with the requirements; or optionality is unstated.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: added the word 'optional' in the subheading of the overview regarding concentrations, to underscore that a concentration is not required.

rules.rule: For multi-campus programs, overview links point to the network-wide listing, not a single campus.
rules.check: Overview link targets a single-campus program when the program is offered at multiple campuses.
rules.why: All network versions should be discoverable.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: revised to a link to the college's professional doctorate programs, where all network versions of the EdD program appear.

rules.rule: If a concentration is not required to complete the program, the heading must not be 'Concentrations' (use 'Concentration or Electives Option') and 'Complete one of the following concentrations' must be removed.
rules.check: Concentration heading/instructions imply a required concentration when it is optional.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: 'Concentrations' heading reverted to 'Concentration or Electives Option', as a concentration is not required for completion of this program.

rules.rule: Populate the internal 'Concentration(s)' field; add NOCC (No Concentration) when none is required; set 'Can students choose this concentration at time of admission?' consistently.
rules.check: Concentration internal field empty/inconsistent; missing NOCC on no-concentration programs.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: NOCC (No Concentration) added to 'Concentration(s)' field, as a concentration is not required to earn the degree nor required to be declared at time of admission.

rules.rule: Inactive courses within a concentration must be resolved before approval.
rules.check: Any course in a concentration/curriculum is inactive.
rules.why: Students can't enroll in inactive courses.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: Proposal moved to CPS dean's office for resolution of inactive courses in Applied Machine Intelligence Concentration.

rules.rule: Concentration requirements should be consistent across a program's campus deployments (align to the Boston record).
rules.check: Non-Boston deployment's concentration requirements differ from the Boston record without cause.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: Update to the Insurance Analytics concentration requirements, per the same concentration's requirements on the Boston record for this program.

rules.rule: Publish only the MINIMUM hours required to complete the program (no ranges), EXCEPT Align/Bridge/Connect programs.
rules.check: Total/required-hours field shows a range (e.g. '34-35 SH') for a non-Align/Bridge/Connect program.
rules.why: Catalog documents the minimum for completion.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: changed to just 34 SH, per current catalog practice to document only the min required hours (except for Align/Bridge/Connect programs).

rules.rule: Choice/restricted-elective language uses 'at least N SH' / 'a minimum of N SH', not a range.
rules.check: Requirement text says 'Complete X-Y SH from the following'.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: 'Complete 4-5 SH from the following...' to 'Complete at least 4 SH from the following...'

rules.rule: Remove 'maximum of N semester hours' statements.
rules.check: Curriculum states a maximum SH a student may complete.
rules.why: Catalog documents the minimum; students may exceed it.

example.program: Accounting and Financial Decision Making, Graduate Certificate
example.author: h.daly
example.quote: removed '...may complete a maximum of 15 semester hours', as the catalog publishes the minimum required for certificate completion.

rules.rule: Credit hours must be semester hours (SH), not quarter hours (QH).
rules.check: Any quarter-hour reference (QH) in requirements or credit/GPA section.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: Quarter hours reference in Program Credit / GPA Requirements section corrected to semester hours.

rules.rule: For 'choose N SH from the following' requirements, place the hours in the dedicated hours field and indent the options (so credit attaches to the requirement, not each option); un-indent core-requirement courses so their hours display.
rules.check: Choice-list options each show credit hours; or core courses are indented and hide hours.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: 3 semester hours added in dedicated hours field ... Course options then indented thereafter, so that 3 SH is associated with the requirement and not with each option.

rules.rule: Any change to core requirements must be routed to UGCC (graduate) / UUCC (undergraduate).
rules.check: Proposal changes core requirements but workflow omits UGCC/UUCC.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: To UGCC for changes to core requirements.

rules.rule: Adding courses from other colleges (or adding/removing a college's course in a UIP) requires UGCC review.
rules.check: Curriculum adds a course owned by another college; confirm UGCC routing.
rules.why: Cross-college course use needs committee sign-off.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: To UGCC for addition of course options from Khoury and Bouve.

rules.rule: A 'Course Not Found' error clears once the referenced new course is approved by UGCC; it is not a program-proposal defect.
rules.check: Curriculum shows 'Course Not Found' for a course pending UGCC approval.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: has now been fully approved by UGCC and the course details will populate in the curriculum by the end of this month.

rules.rule: Online programs do not require GRA review; they route to the Registrar's degree-audit team instead.
rules.check: Online program workflow includes GRA review.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: No GRA review required for Online programs.

rules.rule: Set 'Is this program open for students applying through admissions?' correctly; a program admitting PlusOne students (via Slate) must remain 'Yes' even if closed to external applicants.
rules.check: Admissions-open flag set to 'No' on a program that still admits PlusOne students.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: changed the field ... from 'No' to 'Yes', as ... PlusOne students are indeed presently admitted to graduate programs via Slate.

rules.rule: An inactivation proposal is held until its successor new-program proposal is ready; both advance to the same UGCC meeting.
rules.check: Inactivation with a known successor program: coordinate timing.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: held until the college is ready to advance the successor new MS program proposal ... advanced to the same UGCC meeting.

rules.rule: The 'Final Catalog' field on an inactivation must match the inactivation's effective term (inactivated Fall YYYY -> final catalog (YYYY-1)-YYYY).
rules.check: Final Catalog edition does not correspond to the inactivation effective term.
rules.why: Last catalog year the program is published.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: authorized for inactivation as of Fall 2025, the final catalog was 2024-2025 rather than 2025-2026.

rules.rule: CIP code and campus/modality fields are set by the Registrar's degree-audit team on new records (administrative, not a college action).
rules.check: Do not expect the college to supply CIP; Registrar adds it.

example.author: c.cornwall
example.quote: Registrar's Office administrative action to add CIP Code and campus to new program record fields.

rules.rule: An online program flipping campus BOS -> Online (VTL) for 2026-2027 is not genuinely new even though CourseLeaf tags it 'New Program Proposal'; it's the VTL-campus record creation.
rules.check: 'New Program Proposal' that is actually an existing program changing to Online (VTL).
rules.why: Online students recoded from BOS to VTL as of 2026-2027.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: Although CourseLeaf tags this as a 'New Program Proposal', this program is active and is not new.

rules.rule: Dual-degree programs have no degree-audit impact and skip that step.
rules.check: Dual-degree proposal routed through degree audit unnecessarily.
rules.why: Dual-degree audits handled via component programs.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: No degree audit impacts (dual degree program). Advance to Editor and Catalog Setup.

rules.rule: Credit-bearing experiential-learning courses that also satisfy an elective must be listed in the electives list for degree audits to function.
rules.check: Experiential-learning course fulfills an elective but is absent from the electives list.
rules.why: Degree audit must see the course as an elective option.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: added the credit-bearing courses that fulfill the experiential learning requirement to the electives list ... necessary for proper functioning of future degree audits.

rules.rule: Minimum-grade statements at core requirements use the college's standard wording (e.g. COE: 'must earn a grade of C or higher in all required core courses').
rules.check: Core-requirements min-grade statement missing or non-standard for the college.
rules.why: Consistency across the college's catalog records.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: Min grade in core requirements statement further modified ... per COE approval on other 26-27 records.

rules.rule: Prerequisites outside the program must not be required for core courses; simplify to 'A grade of C or higher is required for each of the following courses.'
rules.check: Core-requirement grade statement imposes external prerequisites.
rules.why: Core requirements are internal to the program.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: prerequisites outside of the program should not be required for core courses.

rules.rule: Do not add 'prerequisite conditions may require a higher minimum grade' when the program has only one core course.
rules.check: Boilerplate multi-course grade sentence on a single-core-course program.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: Second sentence re min grade in core requirements statement removed, as this program has only one core requirement.

rules.rule: When elective options require prerequisites outside the program, add the standard alert language and ensure pathways exist that don't require external coursework.
rules.check: Electives require external prereqs with no student-facing alert.
rules.why: Students must be warned; completion must remain feasible.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: 'Some elective options require completion of prerequisites outside of this program.'

rules.rule: If co-op/experiential participation adds hours or tuition, the Program Requirements must alert students.
rules.check: Co-op adds hours but no alert statement in Program Requirements.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: A statement has been added ... to alert students that additional coursework may be needed for participation in co-op depending on concentration.

rules.rule: Optional experiential learning goes in a dedicated 'Optional Experiential Learning Opportunities' area (added with college authorization).
rules.check: Experiential options scattered rather than in a dedicated area.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: 'Optional Experiential Learning Opportunities' curriculum area added to program requirements per authorization of C. Bolick.

rules.rule: Non-credit or non-existent co-op prep courses are removed; do not list a course that was never created or awards no credit.
rules.check: Curriculum references a co-op prep course that doesn't exist / is non-credit.
rules.why: Only real credit-bearing courses belong in requirements.

example.author: da.rogers
example.quote: removed the line about a non-credit coop course as the course was not created.

rules.rule: Zero-credit special-purpose courses (Thesis Continuation, Research) are removed from elective lists.
rules.check: A 0-credit thesis/research course appears among electives.
rules.why: 0-credit courses don't advance required elective hours.

example.author: m.couch-hrinda
example.quote: INFO 7986 Research and INFO 7996 Thesis Continuation removed ... these 0 credit courses will not advance the student toward ... required elective hours.

rules.rule: A heading offering 'Thesis' must reflect what is actually offered (e.g. 'Capstone or Thesis' -> 'Capstone or Project' when thesis is dropped).
rules.check: Heading lists an option (thesis) the program no longer offers.

example.author: c.cornwall
example.quote: Changed the heading 'Capstone or Thesis' to 'Capstone or Project' as the[sis] is no longer an option.

rules.rule: A thesis sequence relying on a repeatable course requires that course to be UGCC-approved as repeatable first.
rules.check: Thesis sequence assumes repeatability of a non-repeatable course.
rules.why: Course repeatability is a UGCC decision.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: The Thesis Sequence cannot be completed as proposed ... until the department ... receives UGCC approval to change the ARTG 7910 course to a repeatable course.

rules.rule: Changes to shared credits in a dual-degree pathway must go to UGCC.
rules.check: Dual-degree shared-credit change without UGCC routing.

example.author: h.daly
example.quote: To UGCC for change in shared credits in this dual degree pathway.

rules.rule: Dual-degree catalog URLs get a Registrar-established redirect when pages move.
rules.check: Renamed/moved dual-degree page needs a redirect (Registrar handles).

example.author: m.depaula
example.quote: Redirect established from .../dual-degrees/law-llm-business-administration-mba/ to .../dual-degrees/

rules.rule: No duplicate courses in a list; electives kept in alphanumeric order.
rules.check: A course appears twice in the same list; electives out of order.

example.author: c.cornwall
example.quote: Removed one instance of CS 7680 as the course was listed twice in the same course list.

rules.rule: Inactive ('red-boxed') courses must be resolved by the college before approval.
rules.check: Any inactive/red-boxed course in requirements or concentrations.

example.author: da.rogers
example.quote: please address the red-boxed inactive courses in your concentrations.

rules.rule: Remove lines for courses that don't exist (never created).
rules.check: Curriculum references a course with no CIM course record.
rules.why: Only real courses belong in the curriculum.

example.author: da.rogers
example.quote: removed the line about a non-credit coop prep course as it does not exist.

rules.rule: The Registrar assigns the CIP code (choosing a DHS STEM-list code where the program qualifies) and campus/modality fields.
rules.check: Do not supply CIP; note STEM eligibility for the Registrar.

example.author: da.rogers
example.quote: I gave the 30.3301 Sustainability Studies CIP code which also appears on the DHS STEM list.

rules.rule: The Registrar creates the Banner record, incl. a separate Virtual (VTL) record for online; two virtual modalities are distinguished with a 'PO' code suffix.
rules.check: Online program: expect a distinct VTL/PO Banner record created by Registrar.

example.author: da.rogers
example.quote: this program is getting the 'PO' at the end of the code to distinguish the two virtual modalities.

rules.rule: Concentrations are added/removed in Banner to match the approved curriculum; a concentration is unchecked in Banner to prevent admission into it.
rules.check: Banner concentrations must match the curriculum; admission-closed concentrations unchecked.

example.author: da.rogers
example.quote: RABS ... was in Banner already with Machine Learning, so I unchecked it so that no one could be admitted.

rules.rule: For online-only programs the Boston Banner instance is ended as of the conversion term.
rules.check: Online-only program still has an active Boston Banner instance.

example.author: da.rogers
example.quote: Ended Boston instance in Banner for 202710. This program is Online Only.
